campus: Catania — Department of Political and Social Sciences (DSPS), Palazzo Pedagaggi, Via Vittorio Emanuele II 49
admission_type: Open access with verification of curricular requirements and personal preparation. Non-EU applicants residing abroad who require a visa apply through a qualification-based public selection call, with a possible online interview or test.
admission_route: Non-EU citizens residing abroad who require a visa: non_eu_public_selection_call through the UNICT Student Portal, followed by Universitaly pre-enrolment. EU/equated citizens and qualifying non-EU residents in Italy with a foreign qualification: eu_pre_evaluation_webform, followed by the open-access master's admission application through Smart_Edu.
citizenship_track: non_eu_resident_abroad / eu_and_equated / non_eu_resident_in_italy. Italian and EU citizens, citizens of Iceland, Norway, Switzerland, Liechtenstein and San Marino, and non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy for at least one year in the qualifying categories use the same open-access route as Italian applicants.
academic_requirements: A bachelor's degree, three-year university diploma, or another Italian or foreign qualification recognized as suitable is required. Directly eligible Italian degree classes are L-05, L-06, L-11, L-12, L-14, L-16, L-18, L-19, L-20, L-33, L-36, L-37, L-39, L-40, L-42 and LMG/01, including corresponding former-system classes and equivalent pre-reform four-year degrees. Applicants from other degree classes need at least 42 CFU across at least three of the specified M-GGR, M-STO, IUS, SECS-P and SPS disciplinary groups. All eligible applicants remain subject to verification of adequate personal preparation in programme topics, language, international history, political philosophy, social sciences and international relations. For the non-EU-abroad selection, the foreign bachelor's or higher degree must follow at least three years of study and qualify the holder for master's entry in the country of award.
eligible_bachelor_backgrounds: Political Science; EU Studies; International Relations; Diplomatic Studies; Area Studies; Development Studies; cultural and social studies; humanities and history; communication studies; modern languages; international and/or EU law; international and/or EU economics. The 2026/27 Italian annex also accepts the listed Italian degree classes L-05, L-06, L-11, L-12, L-14, L-16, L-18, L-19, L-20, L-33, L-36, L-37, L-39, L-40, L-42 and LMG/01, plus corresponding/equivalent former degrees.
curricular_subject_prerequisites: Applicants holding a degree outside the directly eligible classes must have at least 42 CFU distributed across at least three of these disciplinary-area groups: M-GGR/01–02; M-STO/02–04; IUS/02, 08, 09, 13, 14, 21; SECS-P/01, 02, 04, 12; SPS/01, 02, 04, 06–13. Curricular requirements must be held before the personal-preparation assessment.
degree_recency_limit: No fixed degree-recency exclusion is stated for GLOPEM in the 2026/27 materials.
undergraduate_in_progress_allowed: Yes. Non-EU applicants residing abroad may apply before graduating if they obtain the bachelor's degree by 31 July 2026. Under the open-access route, graduating students may apply conditionally; at 1 October 2026 they must have no more than 30 CFU outstanding, including the final examination, and must have submitted a thesis-assignment request. Conditional enrolment must be finalized by obtaining the degree and all curricular requirements by 28 February 2027.
professional_experience_alternative: Yes, in a limited form. Applicants with a first-level degree outside the listed backgrounds may be considered when they have relevant professional experience aligned with the programme. The non-EU call specifically refers to candidates seconded from international organisations or national foreign services who hold a university degree and have relevant professional experience; the open-access annex also permits relevant work experience in public or private bodies, subject to assessment of personal preparation.
language_requirements: Good written and spoken English at CEFR B2 or higher. The non-EU-abroad selection requires an accepted certificate or exemption evidence. Under the open-access route, B2 can also be verified through an admission language test/interview when it is not demonstrated by an English-taught degree or language-institute certification.

english_certificate_thresholds.cambridge_min: Cambridge First Certificate in English (FCE) or higher

english_certificate_exemptions: A declaration from the university that awarded the bachelor's or master's degree confirming that English was the official language of the programme, or a self-declaration of citizenship of an English-speaking country.
italian_language_requirement: No Italian-language test is required for this fully English-taught master's programme in the 2026/27 non-EU selection. No separate Italian-language admission requirement is stated in the programme-specific open-access annex.
application_deadline_eu: For EU/equated applicants with a foreign qualification, the 2026/27 pre-evaluation form was open from 8 April to 30 June 2026. The subsequent open-access master's admission application through Smart_Edu ran from 6 July to 2 September 2026.
application_deadline_non_eu: 17 March 2026 at 23:59 GMT+1 for the dedicated non-EU applicants residing abroad selection (applications opened 10 February 2026 at 12:00 GMT+1). Visa applicants also had to complete Universitaly pre-enrolment by 31 July 2026.
results_publication_date: By 6 May 2026 for the non-EU-abroad public selection. Under the open-access procedure, applicant lists were due by 4 September 2026 and admitted/not admitted/interview-required lists by 9 September 2026; candidates passing the interview were listed after the 15 September 2026 session.
required_documents: Non-EU-abroad selection: passport personal-data pages; bachelor's degree certificate or enrolment certificate stating expected graduation date; official translation into Italian or English where needed; transcript listing courses, exams, grades, grading range and preferably GPA; official syllabi on university letterhead or validated by university stamp; reference letter, preferably from a university lecturer; Europass-format CV in English; English certificate or exemption evidence; statement of purpose in English (maximum 4,000 characters); summary sheet; and optional supporting documents. EU/equated foreign-degree pre-evaluation: final secondary-school diploma and Declaration of Value or comparability certificate; bachelor's degree and Declaration of Value or comparability/verification certificate; transcript or Diploma Supplement; official stamped and signed course syllabi; motivation letter; professor's recommendation letter; and English certificate. The later Smart_Edu application requires the academic record/self-certification and a valid identity document where applicable.
entry_exam_or_test: Admission normally begins with curriculum and personal-preparation review. For the open-access route, applicants whose preparation or B2 English is not established may be called to an interview. The GLOPEM interview was scheduled for 15 September 2026 at 15:30 at DSPS, Via Vittorio Emanuele II 49, Catania; it checks B2 English where not otherwise proven and assesses personal preparation for candidates relying on a different degree background plus relevant work experience. For the non-EU-abroad selection, qualifications are scored out of 100: academic record up to 50, relevance of prior studies/experience up to 40, reference letter up to 5 and statement of purpose up to 5; the board may require an online interview/test, and 50/100 is the suitability threshold.
credential_recognition_documents: Foreign qualifications must meet UNICT's official country-specific title requirements. Depending on route and stage, applicants may need a Declaration of Value or CIMEA/ENIC-NARIC comparability and verification documentation for the bachelor's degree and the preceding secondary-school qualification, plus official translations. At final enrolment, non-EU visa applicants must deliver a passport copy with study visa, Italian tax code, ENIC/NARIC Statement of Comparability and qualification verification or a Declaration of Value, and the residence-permit request.
tuition_or_fees_link: https://www.unict.it/it/corsi-numero-programmato/2026-2027/public-selection-admission-non-eu-students-living-abroad-english (the linked call states a total 2026/27 tuition/enrolment charge of EUR 306 for non-EU students residing abroad: EUR 140 regional tax, EUR 16 stamp duty and EUR 150 annual comprehensive contribution; EU/equated fees follow the 2026/27 Manifesto degli Studi and contribution regulation).
application_fee: EUR 10 per programme application for the 2026/27 non-EU-abroad selection. The open-access procedure states no application fee, but an additional assessment, if required, incurs EUR 35 charged with the second tuition instalment.
enrolment_confirmation_fee: EUR 75, non-refundable, payable within 15 days of admission notification for admitted non-EU-abroad applicants; it is deducted from the EUR 150 annual comprehensive contribution. Under the open-access route, enrolment requires payment of the EUR 156 fixed charge (EUR 140 regional tax plus EUR 16 stamp duty).
places_quota_non_eu: [uncertain] No programme-specific non-EU seat quota is stated in the public-facing 2026/27 call table; the available-places cell is blank.
places_quota_total: [uncertain] No total capacity is stated; the official 2026/27 programme page and admission procedure classify GLOPEM as open access/non-programmed.
application_portal_url: Non-EU abroad and open-access admission: https://studenti.smartedu.unict.it/ ; EU/equated foreign-qualification pre-evaluation: https://webform.unict.it/en/pre-evaluation-form-english-taught-master-degree-courses-eu-and-equated-citizens-only ; visa pre-enrolment: https://www.universitaly.it/
governing_decree_reference: D.R. 392 of 4 February 2026 (non-EU students residing abroad); D.R. 2233 of 23 June 2026 (open-access two-year master's admission procedure).

uncertainty_notes: The official 2026/27 public-facing non-EU call table leaves the available-places cell blank for GLOPEM, so the previously reported 2025/26 quota cannot be carried forward reliably. No total capacity is published, while the main 2026/27 programme listing and general master's procedure classify the programme as non-programmed/open access. The department's detailed teaching regulation currently available is for the 2025/26 cohort, so current admission facts were taken from the 2026/27 central call and programme-specific annexes. The EUR 306 fee figure is specific to non-EU students residing abroad; Italian/EU/equated contributions follow the broader 2026/27 fee regulation and may differ.
